content: 1. In the weeks following the administration of etrasimod, co-administration with interferon alfa-1 is not recommended. Both drugs may enhance each other's immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. The combination of etrasimod with antineoplastic, immune-modulating, or non-corticosteroid immunosuppressive therapies has not been studied. Therefore, avoid or use alternative drugs during and after etrasimod administration. 2. Etrasimod and interferon beta-1a should not be co-administered. The immunosuppressive effects of both drugs may amplify each other, leading to an increased risk of infection. Avoid or use alternative drugs, as the additive immune system effects of etrasimod in combination with other therapies have not been studied. 3. Co-administration of etrasimod with interferon beta-1b is not advised. The immunosuppressive effects of these drugs may increase the risk of infection. Avoid or use alternative drugs, as the safety of combining etrasimod with other immunosuppressive therapies has not been evaluated. 4. Etrasimod and ipilimumab should not be used together. Their combined immunosuppressive effects may heighten the risk of infection. Avoid or use alternative drugs, as the potential additive immune system effects of etrasimod with other therapies remain unstudied. 5. Irbesartan may increase the levels or effects of etrasimod through mechanisms involving CYP2C9 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs, especially in patients who are poor CYP2C9 metabolizers or are taking moderate-to-strong CYP2C8 inhibitors, as this may lead to increased exposure to etrasimod. 6.
